prompt:
(a) Explain how an experimental result can possess high precision while simultaneously having low accuracy. [2]
(b) Explain how taking repeated readings and calculating their mean affects:
(i) the precision of the individual measurements, [1]
(ii) the accuracy of the final calculated mean when only random errors are present. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Part (a): Precision depends only on the agreement / small spread among repeated readings.
Part (a): A systematic error (such as a zero error or calibration offset) displaces all readings from the true value in the same direction, reducing accuracy without affecting their spread.
Part (b)(i): The precision of the individual measurements is unchanged (their spread remains the same).
Part (b)(ii): The accuracy of the mean improves because random positive and negative variations cancel, bringing the mean closer to the true value.

hints: In part (a), distinguish between spread and offset from true value.
In part (b)(i), does averaging change the scatter of the raw data already taken?
In part (b)(ii), how do random variations behave when summed and averaged?
solution: (a) Precision depends only on the spread among repeated readings. A systematic error shifts all readings in the same direction away from the true value without changing their spread, resulting in high precision but low accuracy. (b)(i) The precision of individual measurements is unchanged. (b)(ii) The accuracy of the mean improves because random variations cancel out, bringing the mean closer to the true value.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) Repeated readings can be clustered tightly (e.g. within 0.01 mm), giving high precision. If an uncorrected zero error of +0.50 mm exists, the entire cluster is displaced from the true value, resulting in low accuracy.
(b)(i) Taking more readings does not alter the spread of individual readings; each still has the same random uncertainty.
(b)(ii) With only random errors, deviations above and below the true value cancel in the sum, making the mean more accurate than a single reading.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored analytical explanation linking systematic and random errors to precision and accuracy evolution.
